cohort: 100 high-risk antenatal women with singleton pregnancies at 35-36 weeks of gestation, complicated by conditions such as GDM, anemia, or hypertensive disorders.
finding: Umbilical cord thickness, fetal fat layer, and shoulder pad thickness are reliable predictors of fetal macrosomia in high-risk pregnancies, with GDM emerging as the strongest maternal risk factor and EFW >4.0 kg predicting macrosomia with 100% accuracy.
mod_finding: Macrosomia was most frequent in Cesarean section deliveries (95%).
